findings.title: Authenticate committed pair bytes before trusting resume coverage
findings.body: PairStore.validate() checks only finiteness and the causal identity, not the identity of the previously committed numeric bytes. For example, changing a finite greater/lesser entry of a committed future-time pair leaves its zero retarded component valid, so resume accepts the changed pair, skips its contraction, and subsequently publishes fresh hashes for the altered data. This shared store also owns cubic old0/new0/family stages. Preserve and authenticate committed-pair digests before adopting bitmap coverage; newly generated final-file hashes cannot authenticate the original commit.

findings.title: Authenticate saved dependency bindings before resuming contractions
findings.body: Resume compares a request binding only joint_blocks.py and produce_joint.py, then overwrites the recorded owning-dependency bindings without authenticating their saved values. Consequently, changing A41's monomial implementation or A50's vertex implementation between invocations leaves committed pairs untouched while remaining pairs use the changed implementation, and the catalog attributes the entire result to the new bindings. cubic_update.py has the same issue at lines 253-255 for ordered_matrix and reference dependencies. Authenticate the previously recorded dependency bindings before reconstruction or further commits, and reject changes instead of replacing their provenance.
